  "text": "Every Tuesday, Ruth took a shirt to the repair shop beneath the railway bridge. The cuffs were sound, but the buttons kept coming loose.

“You could buy stronger thread,” the man behind the counter said.

“I could buy another shirt.”

“That too.”

He wore a tape measure around his neck. One end was shorter than the other.

While he sewed, Ruth stood beside a shelf of unclaimed shoes. There was a red pair with buckles and a single brown boot.

“Who forgets one boot?” she asked.

“Someone with another.”

In May, the shop window filled with a notice announcing repairs to the bridge. Scaffolding covered the entrance. Ruth had to turn sideways between two poles.

“You’ll lose your customers,” she said.

“Some of them know where I am.”

He shook a button tin until he found a match.

The next Tuesday, she brought a cloth and a bottle of window cleaner.

“You can’t see the notice for dust.”

“Nobody reads it.”

“They might if they could.”

He moved the shoes from the sill.

Ruth cleaned the glass inside and out, working around the scaffold poles. Then she put the shoes back, pairing the red ones neatly.

The brown boot had a split lace. She tucked both ends inside.

When she came in again, her shirt lay folded on the counter.

“What do I owe you?”

“Nothing today.”

She reached for her purse anyway.

He held up the window cloth.

“Same time next week?”

Ruth looked at the shirt. He had stitched all the buttons, even the small spare one sewn inside the hem.

“Leave the shoes off the sill,” she said."
